The current 44.55 mL prediction makes this a strong discriminator between loading dependence, interpolation failure, and an exceptional recorded outcome.

This m177 20/1, 150 ul experiment remains unmeasured despite its attribution in previous prose. It contrasts directly with 20/1, 50 ul in aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58 and with 50/1, 150 ul in b514312eda7950cdcf1c, testing whether the large finishing-volume change requires both high loading and the weakest selected mobile phase.

Fill the m146 2/1 loading midpoint at 100 ul. Measured 50 and 150 ul points cf36dbeee8bb51632d84 and 56151359aadfa5411fc6 have V1 values 20.07 and 14.59 mL but nearly identical V2 around 34.2 mL. The complete 5/1 loading series, including 04a2e8ad27ca641a3a12, 51f5ae6a991eea9e720e, and 61b73b8065ae2ece22eb, shows earlier onset at higher loading with a slightly later finish. The m104 5/1, 100 ul point bridges measured 2/1 in dca3d2d055e1cf2d8184 and 50/1 in 302e458c5ed2285ca328. Its predicted early onset and modest finish test whether the unusual methyl anthranilate response persists through intermediate conditions and differs consistently from the ethyl analogue.

Measure m89 at 2/1, 100 ul to connect its measured 5/1 and 50/1 behavior in 5df4935254e8c1e8471d and 249b884b29177edb9df5. It also provides the ortho ethyl aminobenzoate anchor for the selected para and meta experiments at the same mobile-phase ratio and sample volume.

The m89 10/1, 100 ul experiment fills the large gap between measured 5/1 in 5df4935254e8c1e8471d and 50/1 in 249b884b29177edb9df5. It locates the rise toward late retention while the selected m104 midpoint tests whether the methyl analogue follows a fundamentally different recorded response.

Introduce molecule-novel para ethyl aminobenzoate m86 at 2/1, 100 ul. The para, meta, and ortho ethyl isomers share the supplied gross polarity descriptors, yet their predictions differ. This tests positional transfer alongside the selected m88 and m89 points, retaining their different recorded loading-solvent volumes as part of the comparison.

Extend meta ethyl aminobenzoate m88 beyond its measured 1/1 anchor 4cb169fead3b3de5dada. At 2/1, 100 ul it completes the positional comparison with m86 and m89 and tests whether amino-group accessibility and ester context need more specific representations than shared HBD/HBA and TPSA values.

Introduce molecule-novel ether acrylate m20 at 5/1, 100 ul as the first of a matched ratio pair. The extra ether provides a focused structural contrast to labeled acrylates; the substantial retention of aromatic ether acrylate m21 at 50/1 in b4351e5f05f6d477a6c0 shows why transfer of the solvent response deserves direct testing.

Complete the m20 pair at 10/1 with loading held fixed. The model projects V1/V2 increasing from 11.62/18.42 to 20.07/31.76 mL. Measuring both points tests whether an additional ether shifts the response curve coherently, supplying more transferable supervision than an isolated novel-scaffold endpoint.

Introduce molecule-novel methoxybenzyl alcohol m120 at 2/1, 50 ul. It contrasts with methoxyphenethyl alcohol m119 at the same ratio and sample volume in a775926fce57b3bf9ec1, testing how the spacing between the aromatic ring and accessible hydroxyl changes retention rather than relying only on donor and acceptor counts.

Complete the matched m120 2/1-to-5/1 pair. At 5/1 its prediction lies between the recorded responses of methylbenzyl alcohol m135 in f9f0f4e29dbd30c000ee and methoxyphenethyl alcohol m119 in 776ee2c1e85ebde75168, although those references have different loadings. The pair tests whether these structural changes shift the response slope as well as retention level.

Introduce molecule-novel acetylbenzoyl diketone m26 at 5/1, 100 ul. Its structural relationship to m168 and fluorinated m167 makes it a useful test of carbonyl environment and possible tautomer-dependent silica interactions. The earlier transfer failure at acquisition of fa6fd34875fdc7acf6c1 warns against assuming all related diketones develop late onset.

Complete the matched m26 pair at 20/1. The projected change from about 7.08/18.83 to 12.13/34.06 mL tests whether the model transfers a late-response trend appropriately across diketone substitutions. Related measured m168 at 50/1 in e82a87ee526fdd9b1e8d has early onset with an extended finish, so both outputs are informative.

Introduce tertiary amino acrylate m19 at 2/1, 100 ul. Its basic nitrogen and ester distinguish it from the selected neutral ether acrylate m20 and from secondary amine m212, measured at 2/1 in 6defbf00ecb558b77d50. This tests transfer of nitrogen environment and donor absence under a familiar mobile-phase condition.

Introduce low-similarity beta-ketonitrile m47 at 5/1. Its predicted modest retention tests whether replacing an aromatic group or a second carbonyl with a nitrile changes adsorption enough to invalidate transfer from labeled carbonyl/nitrile and diketone families. This fills a functional-group combination poorly represented in the observations.

Introduce pyridyl ketone m66 at 2/1, 100 ul as the first of a matched pair. Pyridyl ester m90 has measured 2/1 behavior in 22f82413c75481d74e9b and strong ratio dependence thereafter. The ketone pair tests whether that response transfers across the carbonyl linkage without assuming identical silica interactions.

Complete the m66 pair at 5/1, predicted at 27.34/62.91 mL. Compare its measured slope with the m90 sequence represented by 22f82413c75481d74e9b and 855832bd4005ac7abdc6. This is a focused test of structure-conditioned solvent response in a basic heteroaromatic region with repeated historical underprediction.

Introduce ether-containing acetoacetate m107 at 5/1, 50 ul. Methyl acetoacetate m95 at the same ratio and sample volume is measured in cd566862a517dd7cdc8d. The extra ether and ester-side-chain change test whether the model can transfer carbonyl-rich retention without conflating it with the much broader finish of m13 in 5d530b2f228ed39ff952.

Introduce low-similarity cyclic ether aldehyde m194 at 1/1, 50 ul. Paired with its selected 5/1 condition, it tests whether ring-constrained ether placement changes the onset and finish response relative to the labeled aromatic ether aldehydes and related cyclic carbonyl compounds.

Complete the matched m194 pair at 5/1, 50 ul. Its predicted 10.41/22.89 mL supplies a moderate-retention structural transfer test. The recorded broad finish of methoxybenzaldehyde m118 at 10/1 in 319e89d7000731f64e7f makes separate supervision of aldehyde onset and finish particularly useful.

Introduce low-similarity fluorobenzyl cyclopropyl ketone m172 at 20/1, 100 ul. Moving the aromatic ring away from the carbonyl and changing its alkyl environment tests a structural interaction absent from the familiar aryl alkyl ketone series. This explores a plausible transfer gap at a well-represented mobile-phase ratio.

Extend dialdehyde m191 from measured 2/1, 150 ul in 53becf1a41d72abcc45a to 5/1 at the same loading. The current model predicts V2 slightly lower despite the weaker mobile phase. This tests a possible plateau or local finishing-volume artifact after the earlier 8.23 mL V2 underprediction.

Extend m201 from measured 2/1, 50 ul in 5067b637ae304dd5924a to 20/1 with loading fixed. Its single nitro group without a carbonyl provides a useful contrast to nitro aldehyde m193, nitro ketone m37, and anomalous m177, testing whether their steep response transfers too broadly.

Measure m208 at 20/1, 50 ul. Relative to measured 5/1 in 1150272392a90f36db05, the model projects a much earlier onset around 3.72 mL but a slightly later finish. The unusual head-specific response could be real or a transfer artifact; the label discriminates without imposing monotonicity as an absolute rule.

Introduce molecule-novel dimethoxybenzene m123 at 5/1, 100 ul as the first of a matched pair. Labeled methyl-substituted dimethoxybenzene m116 and brominated dimethoxybenzene m108 provide close structural context through c3eb276f59965c3608f1 and dbbaf7572643228cf3aa. The pair tests how substitution and ether arrangement affect transfer.

Complete the matched m123 pair at 20/1. The model predicts little onset movement from 5/1 but appreciable finishing-volume growth. Comparison with measured m116 at 20/1 in c3eb276f59965c3608f1 tests whether that flat onset is a valid structural distinction or excessive smoothing across aromatic ether families.

hypotheses.content: Mobile-phase response depends strongly on molecular structure and can be nonlinear. Increasing the PE fraction generally weakens normal-phase elution, but the recorded response need not be monotonic for every molecule and loading context.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched intermediate-ratio labels teach structure-specific slope and curvature, helping the model transfer condition response rather than apply a global solvent correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which response patterns transfer across pyridyl carbonyls, ether acrylates, diketones, alcohols, and aromatic ethers, and which require more specific structural context?

hypotheses.content: The m177 finishing-volume discontinuity at 50/1 remains unresolved: measured V2 changes from 7.31 mL at 100 ul to 81.30 mL at 150 ul. A loading-dependent regime, an exceptional recorded outcome, and poor model interpolation remain competing explanations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The current broad finishing-volume prediction can spread an exceptional label across neighboring rows. Correctly locating this behavior matters more than applying a general tail adjustment.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: What happens at 50/1 with 50 ul and at 20/1 with 150 ul? These conditions constrain the loading-by-ratio surface, although they cannot alone establish the repeatability of the exceptional 150 ul result.

hypotheses.content: Recorded matched loading series show family- and ratio-dependent associations with V1 and V2. In particular, loading can move onset substantially while leaving finishing volume nearly unchanged; many current candidate predictions are almost invariant to loading.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Loading-insensitive predictions can miss systematic within-family differences even when the structure and ratio are familiar. These observations establish associations, while measurement variability limits purely causal interpretations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m146 loading midpoint at 2/1 preserve the onset shift without changing V2, and does the loading association observed at 5/1 persist at 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Structural novelty has uneven predictive consequences. Targeted changes in functional-group combination, accessibility, or connectivity are more useful acquisition guides than novelty alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Novel-scaffold labels should teach reusable structural distinctions. Paired conditions and close functional contrasts can reveal transfer failures even when single-point predictions appear ordinary.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which changes most disrupt transfer: tertiary amine versus ether, nitrile versus carbonyl, alcohol spacing, constrained ether placement, or carbonyl substitution in related diketones?

hypotheses.content: Onset and finishing-volume responses can decouple, so a shared shift or scale correction cannot reliably repair both outputs. Predicted bends and reversals should be checked separately for each head.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels around onset and finish transitions supervise distinct output errors and prevent interval width from acting as a substitute for either target.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m11 and m80 transitions, m191 finishing-volume plateau, m208 onset decrease, and m123 nearly flat onset survive measurement?

hypotheses.content: Aminobenzoate retention may require positional and ester-alkyl context together with recorded loading conditions. The large ortho methyl/ethyl difference is observed, but it cannot yet be assigned solely to ester alkyl identity because the loading contexts also differ.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Closely related isomers share gross descriptors but differ in possible intramolecular interactions and silica accessibility. Intermediate labels can prevent both excessive pooling and unjustified scaffold-specific extrapolation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 2/1, how do the para, meta, and ortho ethyl contexts differ, and do m104 at 5/1 and m89 at 10/1 maintain their distinct recorded response patterns?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback supports local response experiments but requires correcting the earlier interpretation using the observed table. Outcome 5e2f71c50a4ccaa1b83e is m45 at 1/1 and 50 ul, not m177 at 20/1; 5b7c4a47b624119302fa is m127 at 0/1, not m177 at 50/1; and dbbaf7572643228cf3aa is m108 at 50/1, not m72 at 2/1. Their historical errors therefore do not resolve the previously proposed m177 or m72 contrasts. The selected m177 conditions address two gaps that remain genuinely open. Also, PE/EA 0/1 is pure EA and the strongest mobile-phase endpoint, correcting earlier descriptions of it as low strength. The m146 loading series and the m205 1/1 outcomes strengthen evidence for family-dependent loading associations, while 8b09df1985688231fe0e reinforces separate onset and finish calibration. Novel-transfer outcomes were mixed: the dialdehyde 53becf1a41d72abcc45a had substantial V2 underprediction, whereas brominated ester 381a7717cd8db0a06c69 was predicted closely. This shifts exploration toward explicit functional contrasts and linked conditions rather than novelty or broad quantile spans alone.
batch_rationale: The batch combines correction of unresolved failure regions with experiments that can teach reusable structure-condition relationships. The two m177 points discriminate explanations for an exceptional finishing-volume discontinuity. The m146 points constrain loading associations, and matched m11 and m80 ratio pairs locate transitions in both outputs. Five aminobenzoate experiments examine a striking structural-context discrepancy through intermediate conditions. New-scaffold ratio pairs for m20, m120, m26, m66, m194, and m123 make exploration informative about response slope as well as retention level; single anchors for m19, m47, m107, and m172 cover specific connectivity and functional-group gaps. Finally, m191, m201, and m208 extend sparsely observed families where current predictions raise distinct questions about carbonyl multiplicity, nitro-group context, and onset/finish decoupling. These choices span early, moderate, and late regimes without seeking large retention volumes themselves. Repeated catalog tuples were avoided within the batch, and numerical novelty, CW distance, and quantile spans were used only alongside chemical and measured evidence. The expected benefit is better transfer and interpolation across the Row-distribution, including regions whose ordinary-looking predictions may conceal structural or loading errors.
